title: Sid Meier: Gamers Aren't Logical (Game Informer report of GDC 2010 keynote)
label: developer
claim: Secondhand press report, no direct Meier quote on odds. Civ Revolution testers: wins at 3-to-1 felt fair; even 1-to-3 wins excited players; losses at 2-to-1 were accepted but losing a 20-to-10 fight upset players ('It's 20-to-10! I should win! It's a big number!') though mathematically the same ratio. Team concluded the battle system could not be pure math. Press accounts differ on how the odds were framed.

title: GDC10 Notes: Sid Meier (attendee notes)
label: snippet
claim: Search summary only: Meier said odds had to be made 'even odder' to match players' sense of fairness. Not read; primary GDC talk not reached.

title: Liquipedia Dota 2: Random Distribution
label: practitioner
claim: Fetch returned 403. Via search snippet only: all chance-based crit sources use pseudo-random distribution; chance starts below the listed rate and rises after each failed attempt, resets on success. Example figures (Bash ~8.5% reset, third attack ~25.5%) came from secondary translated sites, not verified. Fan wiki, not Valve.

title: Zendle & Cairns 2018, Video game loot boxes are linked to problem gambling (PLOS ONE)
label: research
claim: Survey of 7,422 gamers. Loot box spending vs problem gambling severity eta-squared 0.054; other real-money in-game item spending eta-squared 0.004. Correlational: authors state it is unclear whether loot boxes are a gateway or problem gamblers are drawn to them.

title: Spicer et al. 2022, Loot boxes, problem gambling and problem video gaming: systematic review and meta-synthesis (New Media & Society 24(4))
label: snippet
claim: Fetched page held only bibliographic data (GambleAware funded). Figures from search summary of the abstract: 13 publications on loot boxes vs problem gambling, 12 positive, mean r = .27; loot boxes vs problem video gaming mean r = .40 from six surveys; authors say causal direction still unestablished.

title: Spicer et al. 2022 Addictive Behaviors, gateway hypothesis
label: snippet
claim: Survey of 1,102 loot box purchasers who also gamble; gateway effects reported in both directions, associated with higher problem-gambling scores. Search summary only.

title: PCGamesN: secret dice rolls in XCOM Enemy Within
label: developer
claim: Reports lead designer Anand Gupta describing a hidden luck modifier overriding displayed hit chance: a 'bad streak breaker' on Normal and Easy, stronger on Easy, grows as soldiers are lost; on Easy a player who misses three times in a row will not miss a fourth even at 1%. Absent on Classic and higher. Secondhand report of a developer statement; fetch summariser output.

title: PC Gamer: Dispatch cheats random percentages in the player's favor
label: opinion

title: Hearthstone wiki: Card pack statistics (cites Blizzard)
label: practitioner
claim: Fan wiki citing Blizzard: 2023 support article says a Legendary is guaranteed within 40 packs of the previous Legendary; one Legendary guaranteed within first 10 packs of a new expansion (2017 blog); counters per set; golden packs also have pity timers; 2017 change means Legendaries from a pack are ones you do not own until you own all of the set. Hearthstone drop rates were first posted on a Chinese site in 2017 for legal compliance. Blizzard primary pages not read.

title: Fire Emblem Wiki: True hit
label: practitioner
claim: 2RN averages two rolls and compares to displayed hit. 2RN displayed to true: 10 to 2.10, 20 to 8.20, 30 to 18.30, 40 to 32.40, 50 to 50.50, 60 to 68.40, 70 to 82.30, 80 to 92.20, 90 to 98.10. 1RN (displayed = true) through Thracia 776; 2RN Binding Blade to Awakening and Three Houses; hybrid in Fates, Shadows of Valentia, Engage: below 50 shown truthfully, 50+ single roll with a curve (90 displays 97.05 true). Fan wiki reverse engineering, not designer statement; no stated designer rationale.

title: Diplograph note: lying about probability
label: opinion
claim: Blog argues 2RN makes attacks feel more predictable so stats matter more than luck; Advance Wars 2 damage preview shows minimum with luck on top. Cites fan wikis; no designer quotes.

title: Zhang, Monteiro, Liang et al., Effect of Input-output Randomness on Gameplay Satisfaction in Collectable Card Games
label: research
claim: Within-subject, n=18 college students, 4 conditions (none, input, output, both) in a custom card game, GUESS questionnaire, online, 15 min per condition over 4 days. Input randomness (mystery cards) lowered satisfaction (F(1,15)=6.275, p=0.024, partial eta-sq 0.295); output randomness had no significant effect (p=0.859); authors say likely underpowered, one genre, and result contradicts the common view that input randomness is the good kind. Participants said no-input-randomness modes allowed more strategic planning; one found them too easy.

title: Keith Burgun, Randomness and Game Design (Game Developer, 2014)
label: practitioner
claim: Output randomness = noise between a player's choice and its result (Risk, X-Com dice combat); input randomness informs the player before deciding (Civ/Rogue map generation, Puerto Rico face-up tiles). He favors well-balanced low-variance input randomness in multiplayer, says single-player needs input randomness, says the two sit on a continuum and badly used input randomness causes the same problems. His thesis: output randomness does not belong in strategy games.

title: Fabian Fischer, Sources of uncertainty (Game Developer, 2015)
label: practitioner
claim: Cites Costikyan only as a source, no Costikyan quote. Input randomness gives new situations; output randomness 'will in general lead to unfair results' and distorts feedback, hurting learning. Complexity alone 'is generally not enough'.

title: Belgian Gaming Commission April 2018 loot box report (via press)
label: snippet
claim: Via search summaries: commission found paid loot boxes in Overwatch, FIFA 18 and CS:GO meet the elements of a game of chance (game, wager, chance, win/loss); Battlefront II cleared after its system changed; threat of up to five years prison and EUR 800,000 fine; only four games examined; report in Dutch with English translation.

title: China forces game producers to reveal loot box odds (Engadget, Dec 2016)
label: snippet
claim: Via search summaries: Ministry of Culture rule published Dec 2016, in force 1 May 2017; operators must publish odds of each randomized item on the game's official site; compliance early was mixed (Riot published, Valve paused Dota 2 loot purchases in China). A later study cited by a search summary found only 5 of 100 top iOS games in China show odds automatically (unverified).

title: PC Gamer: Behind the addictive psychology of loot boxes (Luke Clark quoted)
label: snippet
claim: Clark quoted: modern games amplify variable ratio schedules by having many overlapping ones. Search summary found no study directly testing that Skinner-box schedule effects transfer to loot boxes in humans; the link is inference from animal learning work.

title: 80.lv: Jake Solomon on missing shots in XCOM (Midnight Suns context)
label: developer
claim: Solomon: 'when I missed shots, I was unbelievably frustrated' and it was tough to accept that 'in XCOM, you can actually do things wrong'; contrasts Midnight Suns where attacks always land. No percentages given.

title: CogConnected: 5 Ways XCOM 2 Warps Your Sense of Probability
label: developer

title: Derek Yu, Spelunky excerpt (Game Developer, from Boss Fight Books)

Excerpt does not discuss luck vs skill or fairness. Quotes passed through a summariser, so wording is unverified verbatim.
